rubric_fields.label: Originalidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Identifique a contribuição e diferencie-a de conhecimento já estabelecido. Exija evidência no artigo para a alegação de novidade, sem presumir que novidade implique qualidade.

rubric_fields.label: Solidez
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confronte conclusões com métodos, dados ou demonstrações apresentados. Verifique hipóteses, limitações e se o desenho permite a inferência alegada; adapte a exigência ao tipo de artigo.

rubric_fields.label: Substância
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique se experimentos, provas, síntese ou análise sustentam a contribuição declarada. Considere a profundidade e a cobertura da evidência, sem confundir extensão do texto com substância.

rubric_fields.label: Clareza
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique definições, organização e correspondência entre texto, tabelas e figuras. Aponte ambiguidades localizáveis e distinga problemas de redação de problemas científicos.

rubric_fields.label: Comparação
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confira se os trabalhos e alternativas relevantes são discutidos de forma justa. Compare métodos, condições e limitações equivalentes; não exija experimentos de um artigo estritamente teórico.

rubric_fields.label: Impacto
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Relacione a contribuição a uma necessidade da área e ao alcance sustentado pelos resultados. Distinga relevância demonstrada de aplicações futuras ainda especulativas.

rubric_fields.label: Reprodutibilidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique disponibilidade ou descrição suficiente de materiais, dados, procedimentos e parâmetros. Restrições éticas ou legais podem justificar acesso controlado; não exija divulgação de dados pessoais.

document_map.abstract: We propose a simple algorithm to train stochastic neural networks to draw sam- ples from given target distributions for probabilistic inference. Our method is based on iteratively adjusting the neural network parameters so that the output changes along a Stein variational gradient (Liu & Wang, 2016) that maximumly decreases the KL divergence with the target distribution. Our method works for any target distribution specified by their unnormalized density function, and can train any black-box architectures that are differentiable in terms of the parame- ters we want to adapt. As an application of our method, we propose an amor- tized MLE algorithm for training deep energy model, where a neural sampler is adaptively trained to approximate the likelihood function. Our method mimics an adversarial game between the deep energy model and the neural sampler, and obtains realistic-looking images competitive with the state-of-the-art results.

sections.title: 1 INTRODUCTION
sections.first_sentence: Modern machine learning increasingly relies on highly complex probabilistic models to reason about uncertainty.

sections.title: 2 STEIN VARIATIONAL GRADIENT DESCENT (SVGD)
sections.first_sentence: Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD) (Liu & Wang, 2016) is a general purpose Bayesian infer-ence algorithm motivated by Stein's method (Stein, 1972; Barbour & Chen, 2005) and kernelized Stein discrepancy (Liu et al., 2016; Chwialkowski et al., 2016; Oates et al., 2014).

sections.title: 3 AMORTIZED SVGD: TOWARDS AN AUTOMATIC NEURAL SAMPLER
sections.first_sentence: SVGD and other particle-based methods become inefficient when we need to repeatedly infer a large number different target distributions for multiple tasks, including online learning or inner loops of other algorithms, because they can not improve based on the experience from the past tasks, and may require a large memory to restore a large number of particles.

sections.title: 4 AMORTIZED MLE FOR GENERATIVE ADVERSARIAL TRAINING
sections.first_sentence: Our method allows us to design efficient approximate sampling methods adaptively and automat-ically, and enables a host of novel applications.

sections.title: 5 EMPIRICAL RESULTS
sections.first_sentence: We evaluated our SteinGAN on four datasets, MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA (Liu et al., 2015), and Large-scale Scene Understanding (LSUN) (Yu et al., 2015), on which we find our method tends to generate realistic-looking images competitive with, sometimes better than DCGAN (Radford et al., 2015) (see Figure 2 - Figure 3).

sections.title: 6 CONCLUSION
sections.first_sentence: We propose a new method to train neural samplers for given distributions, together with a new SteinGAN method for generative adversarial training.
